description: We are a team of three students passionate about technology, creativity and game development.We like turning challenging ideas into interactive and creative experiences.Our best skills are programming, problem-solving, and design. We are excited to use NASA's data and resources to bring our ideas to life with creativity.
summary:
SOL ZERO is a 3D space mission game built in Unreal Engine. The player lands at an abandoned Mars colony with one companion: S.T.E.L.L.A., the station’s witty AI, who narrates every step by voice. To restore the colony, the player must repair the communication dishes by making a real engineering decision — a quick battery fix or a permanent solar panel cleaning — then complete NASA’s first mission: collecting samples in Jezero Crater, an ancient lake bed. Returning to base, low oxygen forces the player to start MOXIE, modeled on the real Perseverance experiment that produced oxygen from Martian CO2.

The game addresses the challenge by turning mission design trade-offs — temporary vs. root-cause fixes, power, oxygen, communication — into decisions the player feels, with Stella explaining why each choice matters. Facts from NASA’s MOXIE archive, ESA Mars Express observations of Jezero, and NASA mission design documents are woven into dialogue and info cards, so players learn real planetary science and systems engineering by playing — not reading.
details:
SOL ZERO is a 3D narrative mission game built in Unreal Engine. The player lands at an abandoned Mars colony guided by S.T.E.L.L.A., the station’s witty AI, fully voice-acted. The colony’s communication dishes are down, and the player must make a real engineering decision: hook up a backup battery (fast, but temporary) or clean the dust off the solar panels (slower, but it fixes the root cause). Once contact with NASA is restored, the first mission begins: drive the rover to Jezero Crater — an ancient lake bed — and dig for surface samples. Back at base, low oxygen blocks the door until the player starts MOXIE, inspired by the real Perseverance experiment that produced oxygen from Martian CO2.

How we built it: We sculpted and painted the Martian terrain with Unreal’s Landscape tools, created the rocket landing and takeoff cutscenes with Sequencer, built a fully drivable rover on the Chaos Vehicles system, added a digging system for sample extraction, and developed the HUD with UMG widgets. All gameplay logic is in Blueprints. Stella’s voice was generated with ElevenLabs.

Benefits and impact: Space mission design is usually taught as theory. SOL ZERO makes its trade-offs physical: the player feels why a quick fix costs more later, why power constrains everything, and why oxygen is a mission resource. Real facts from NASA’s MOXIE experiment, ESA Mars Express observations of Jezero, and NASA mission design documents are delivered through Stella’s dialogue, so players absorb planetary science while playing.

Creativity: Instead of another survival game, the player restores an abandoned colony — the tension comes from engineering decisions, not danger. Our team balanced scientific accuracy, accessibility for players with no space background, and a scope we could polish within the hackathon.
dataRefs: NASA PDS Atmospheres Node – MOXIE (Mars Oxygen ISRU Experiment)
